nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the primary use of first cut SPL?
nodes.answer: First cut SPL is mainly used for energy purposes in the production of cement, steel, and mineral wool.
nodes.paragraph: According to International Aluminium [8]40 to 50 pct of the SPL is recycled/reused in other processes today, where rst cutis mainly used for energy purposes in the production of cement, steel and mineral wool. Second cut SPL is also used for cement production. In all cases the rst cut SPLhas replaced fossil coal or coke. For both cement and steel, the substitution has given an environmental bene t for both industries. Further, for steel making, a costbene t has also been seen. From the examples given byInternational Aluminium, both the aluminum industryand the end-users can bene t both environmentally and economically from developing cost-e ective alternatives to deposit in land Ils. Several methods for puri cation of SPL have been investigated in literature. Chen et al. [13] ]proposes a method named oxidation-expansion acid leaching (OEAL) which is a novel leaching process for removalof impurities inside graphitized carbon. They suggest that the OEAL manages to remove up to 99 pct of the electrolyte remains in the SPL, as compared to 89 pctwhen using conventional leaching. Rio Tinto has devel-oped a method called the low-caustic leaching and liming process (LCL&L), and this process is industrial- ized today.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What are the types of materials referred to as traditional anode materials?
nodes.answer: Traditional anode materials include metallic materials like sheet copper and stainless steel, as well as carbonaceous materials such as flake graphite, carbon paper, carbon cloth, carbon brush, and carbon rods.
nodes.paragraph: The term traditional anode materials refers to both metallic (such as sheet copper and stainless steel) and carbonaceous (such as flake graphite, carbon paper, carbon cloth, carbon brush, and carbon rods) materials [21]. This is due to the high con- ductivity and chemical stability of carbon rods and flake graphite, the huge specific surface areas of carbon cloth and 345 Bioprocess and Biosystems Engineering (2025) 48:343 366 paper, and the corrosion resistance of stainless steel [22]. Flake graphite and carbon rods are also reasonably priced and readily available. However, there are disadvantages to the materials listed as well. For instance, carbon paper is brittle, stainless steel and carbon cloth are expensive, and metallic and carbonaceous materials lack sufficient electro- chemical active sites to facilitate the process of extracellular electron transfer (EET) between anode and exoelectrogens [23]. Because of their flat surface, which decreases contact area and makes them less compatible with electrochemically active microbes, MFCs are relatively ineffective. The main purpose of the anode is to encourage the establishment of biofilms and raise the likelihood of EET because the anodic reaction in MFCs is dependent on both the metabolic rate of the bacteria (biocatalysis) and the efficiency of electrode interfacial charge transfer (electrocatalysis) [24].

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable materials for energy production_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the significance of developing low-cost biomass-based carbon materials?
nodes.answer: Developing low-cost and renewable biomass-based carbon materials is important for their use in energy storage devices.
nodes.paragraph: It also exhibited a capacity retention of up to 89.72% over 1000 cycles. Keywords Microalgae Pyrolysis lodine and sulphur doping Hydrothermal heating Supercapacitor 1 Introduction Energy, which is vital for world life, seriously affects the economies and the environment of countries around the world due to the current dependence on non-renewable fos- sil fuels [1]. Interest in renewable, environmentally friendly, high-performance energy storage devices such as batteries, supercapacitors and fuel cells for electrochemical energy, which is an important part of clean energy, tends to increase [2, 3]. Among these, supercapacitors, in particular, have gar - nered significant interest from researchers [4 6]. The excellent microstructure and reasonable pore size dis- tribution of biomass-derived carbon materials enable their use in various applications. In particular, the outstanding charge storage/release capacity and high cycling stability of carbon-based supercapacitors promote their applications in energy storage and conversion [7 ]. The development of low- cost and renewable biomass-based carbon materials for use in energy storage devices is an important issue. As typical electrode material for supercapacitors, biomass-based car - bon precursors are attracting intense interest as a reliable and readily available source [8 12].

nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why are fossil fuels considered the backbone of the chemical production and fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Fossil fuels are essential energy and carbon sources for producing textiles and other products in the fashion industry.

nodes.question: What issues do many thermoelectric materials face that limit their large-scale usage?
nodes.answer: Many thermoelectric materials contain toxic and costly elements, which limit their usage on a large scale.
nodes.paragraph: However, many of these materials contain toxic and costly elements, which limit their usage on a large scale. 13 To address this problem, scientists have been searching for thermoelectric materi- als that are abundant, low-cost, and nontoxic. 13 The efforts in this research direction have resulted in the discovery of promising candidates such as Al-Fe-Si,14 Fe-V-Al,15,16 and Cu-S.17 In particular, due to the presence of the pseudo-gap, the Fe-V-AI alloy18 is considered a very promising thermo- electric material, with a power factor of 55 10 4 W/m K2 at room temperature. nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable materials for energy production_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is suggested as the focus of further research to improve the novel biocomposite's competitiveness?
nodes.answer: Further research should focus on minimizing the energy demand associated with AgNP synthesis.
nodes.paragraph: To further enhance antibacterial proper - ties and sustainability performance, a novel biocomposite based on PLA with hemp hurd filled with silver nanoparticles (AgNP) was developed. Here we present a life cycle assessment (LCA) based on ISO 14040 and 14044 to evaluate the added value of the antibacterial biocomposite compared to conventional antibacterial materials from an environmental perspective. The environmental impacts are analyzed in comparison to virgin PLA, fossil-based polypropylene (PP) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) combined in a disinfecting wipes and sterilized application. Our results show that the novel biocomposite has in general higher environmental impacts than its counterparts. Notably, our findings suggest a significant impact derived from high energy demand required for AgNP synthesis. To be able to compete with other materials, the energy demand needs to be minimized, which should be the focus of further research. nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why do textiles made from synthetic fibres have a higher climate impact compared to those made from natural fibres?
nodes.answer: Textiles made from synthetic fibres have a higher climate impact because of their fossil fuel origin and the energy consumed during production.

nodes.question: What materials are used in the production stage of the product life cycle?
nodes.answer: In the production stage of the product life cycle, 200 kg raw cotton, 5000 kW h energy, 1000 l water, and various chemicals are used.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable materials for energy production_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is the production of synthetic fibres like polyester considered less sustainable?
nodes.answer: The polymerization, spinning, and finishing of synthetic fibres such as polyester consume a substantial amount of energy, making them less sustainable compared to natural fibres.
